    Troubleshooting

    Device doesn't appear in the list

    • Make sure your computer and the device are on the same Wi-Fi network. Guest networks or networks that block device-to-device traffic may prevent discovery.
    • Make sure Wireless debugging is on. It can turn off when the device locks or changes networks.
    • Make sure the device runs Android 11 or newer. See Requirements.

    Device name or API isn't shown

    Platform-Tools in Unity's Android SDK is below 36. Install the latest version with Update Platform-Tools.

    "Can't reach the adb server"

    The window connects to the running adb server (127.0.0.1:5037 by default) to find devices. If the server doesn't respond, it starts one with the newest installed adb.

    • If it still can't connect, click Open Preferences… and set the adb path yourself.
    • Make sure a firewall or security software isn't blocking adb.

    List briefly empties or the connection drops

    This can happen when Unity and another tool (such as Android Studio) keep stopping and restarting each other's adb server.

    • If Preferences > External Tools > Kill external ADB instances is on, Unity stops adb servers that aren't from its own SDK. Turn it off if you use other tools at the same time.
    • If Unity's SDK and the other tool use different Platform-Tools versions, they restart each other's server. Update Unity's SDK, or point Preferences > External Tools > Android SDK at the same SDK.

    "Android Build Support isn't installed"

    Add the Android Build Support module to your editor version in Unity Hub, then restart the editor.

    Other issues

    See Troubleshoot wireless connection in the Android documentation.
